;0x00002105;((self.$R=self.$R||{})["server-fn:0"]=[],($R=>$R[0]={question:$R[1]={id:101861527,program:102,test:2,skill:9,difficulty:2,isLive:!1,multiChoice:!0,updateDate:$R[2]=new Date("2023-08-02T20:25:59.632Z"),createDate:$R[3]=new Date("2023-08-02T20:25:59.632Z"),externalId:null,ibn:"070903-DC",stem:"\x3Ctable align=\"center\" border=\"1\" cellpadding=\"1\" cellspacing=\"1\" style=\"width: 25%;\">\x3Cthead>\x3Ctr>\x3Cth scope=\"col\" style=\"text-align: center;\">Species of tree\x3C/th>\x3Cth scope=\"col\" style=\"text-align: center;\">Growth factor\x3C/th>\x3C/tr>\x3C/thead>\x3Ctbody>\x3Ctr>\x3Ctd>Red maple\x3C/td>\x3Ctd style=\"text-align: center;\">4.5\x3C/td>\x3C/tr>\x3Ctr>\x3Ctd>River birch\x3C/td>\x3Ctd style=\"text-align: center;\">3.5\x3C/td>\x3C/tr>\x3Ctr>\x3Ctd>Cottonwood\x3C/td>\x3Ctd style=\"text-align: center;\">2.0\x3C/td>\x3C/tr>\x3Ctr>\x3Ctd>Black walnut\x3C/td>\x3Ctd style=\"text-align: center;\">4.5\x3C/td>\x3C/tr>\x3Ctr>\x3Ctd>White birch\x3C/td>\x3Ctd style=\"text-align: center;\">5.0\x3C/td>\x3C/tr>\x3Ctr>\x3Ctd>American elm\x3C/td>\x3Ctd style=\"text-align: center;\">4.0\x3C/td>\x3C/tr>\x3Ctr>\x3Ctd>Pin oak\x3C/td>\x3Ctd style=\"text-align: center;\">3.0\x3C/td>\x3C/tr>\x3Ctr>\x3Ctd>Shagbark hickory\x3C/td>\x3Ctd style=\"text-align: center;\">7.5\x3C/td>\x3C/tr>\x3C/tbody>\x3Cp>&nbsp;\x3C/p>\x3C/table>\x3Cp>One method of calculating the approximate age, in years, of a tree of a particular species is to multiply the diameter of the tree, in inches, by a constant called the growth factor for that species. The table above gives the growth factors for eight species of trees. If a white birch tree and a pin oak tree each now have a diameter of 1&nbsp;foot, which of the following will be closest to the difference, in inches, of their diameters 10 years from now? (1 foot&nbsp;=&nbsp;12 inches)\x3C/p>",rationale:"\x3Cp>Choice C is correct. According to the given information, multiplying a tree species&rsquo; growth factor by the tree&rsquo;s diameter is a method to approximate the age of the tree. A white birch with a diameter of 12 inches (or 1 foot) has a given growth factor of 5 and is approximately 60 years old. A pin oak with a diameter of 12 inches (or 1 foot) has a given growth factor of 3 and is approximately 36 years old. The diameters of the two trees 10 years from now can be found by dividing each tree&rsquo;s age in 10 years, 70 years, and 46 years, by its respective growth factor. This yields 14 inches and \x3Cspan>\x3Cimg align=\"middle\" role=\"math\" class=\"math-img\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\" alt=\"15 and one third\">\x3C/span> inches. The difference between \x3Cspan>\x3Cimg align=\"middle\" role=\"math\" class=\"math-img\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\" alt=\"15 and one third\">\x3C/span> and 14 is \x3Cspan>\x3Cimg align=\"middle\" role=\"math\" class=\"math-img\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\" alt=\"1 and one third\">\x3C/span>, or approximately 1.3 inches.\x3C/p>\x3Cp>Alternate approach: Since a white birch has a growth factor of 5, the age increases at a rate of 5 years per inch or, equivalently, the diameter increases at a rate of \x3Cspan>\x3Cimg align=\"middle\" role=\"math\" class=\"math-img\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\" alt=\"one fifth\">\x3C/span> of an inch per year. Likewise, the pin oak has a growth factor of 3, so its diameter increases at a rate of \x3Cspan>\x3Cimg align=\"middle\" role=\"math\" class=\"math-img\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\" alt=\"one third\">\x3C/span> of an inch per year. Thus, the pin oak grows \x3Cspan>\x3Cimg align=\"middle\" role=\"math\" class=\"math-img\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\" alt=\"two fifteenths\">\x3C/span> of an inch per year more than the white birch. In 10 years it will grow \x3Cspan>\x3Cimg align=\"middle\" role=\"math\" class=\"math-img\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\" alt=\"two fifteenths times 10, equals four thirds\">\x3C/span> of an inch more, which is approximately 1.3 inches.\x3C/p>\x3Cp>Choices A, B, and D are incorrect and a result of incorrectly calculating the diameters of the two trees in 10 years.\x3C/p>\x3Cp>\x3C/p>"},answers:$R[4]=[$R[5]={id:14075,question:101861527,correct:!1,content:"\x3Cp>1.0\x3C/p>\n"},$R[6]={id:14076,question:101861527,correct:!1,content:"\x3Cp>1.2\x3C/p>\n"},$R[7]={id:14077,question:101861527,correct:!0,content:"\x3Cp>1.3\x3C/p>\n"},$R[8]={id:14078,question:101861527,correct:!1,content:"\x3Cp>1.4\x3C/p>\n"}],userData:void 0})($R["server-fn:0"]))
